options.text: One failure tying up a caller's resources and taking it down, which takes its callers down, spreading across the system
A single server crash with no wider effect

questions.explanation: A cascade is when one slow or failed dependency exhausts a caller's resources, dragging down everything that depends on it — the failure most resilience patterns aim to contain.

questions.prompt: In the OPEN state, what does a circuit breaker do?

options.text: Fails fast — rejects calls immediately without hitting the dependency — for a cooldown period

questions.explanation: When open, the breaker fails fast so callers don't pile up on a down dependency, giving it room to recover. After a cooldown it goes half-open to test recovery.

questions.prompt: What does the bulkhead pattern isolate?

options.text: Resources like thread/connection pools, so one hung dependency can't exhaust all of them

questions.explanation: Bulkheads give each dependency its own resource pool, so a single hung dependency exhausts only its pool and the others keep working — like watertight ship compartments.

questions.prompt: A product page's recommendation service is down. Graceful degradation means:

options.text: Return a 500 error for the whole page
Render the product page without recommendations instead of failing entirely

questions.explanation: Graceful degradation returns a reduced but working response — here, the product page minus the optional recommendations section — rather than failing the whole request.

questions.prompt: What problem does service discovery solve?

options.text: Finding a healthy instance of a dependency at runtime as instances come and go

questions.explanation: Instances constantly change (autoscaling, deploys, failures), so addresses aren't fixed. Service discovery (a registry, DNS, or platform mechanism) returns healthy instances at runtime.

questions.prompt: Under severe overload, why might a system deliberately reject some requests (load shedding)?

options.text: Because serving all requests badly can collapse the system; shedding excess protects the core so most requests succeed

questions.explanation: Trying to serve everything under overload can cause total collapse. Load shedding sacrifices some (often low-priority) requests to keep the core healthy for the rest.
